# **What is Mavigator?**

Mavigator is an iOS and Android app built with React Native (Expo) \[1\] aimed to help UTA students find their way around campus, guide them through indoor room routing, and assist in finding ideal parking spaces.

# Project Plan

Classes are automatically sorted by time and labeled Upcoming, In Progress, or Done based on the current time. |

# **What’s Changed Since Inception?**

Our inception plan initially had three goals for iteration 1: set up a cross-platform framework, define node and edge data interfaces, and start mapping rooms inside Nedderman Hall. While the cross-platform framework has been completed, there is still a majority of the map not completed. We had initially believed that getting the map of campus outdoors would not be difficult because we would just use Google Maps API, but we realized this would not work for our particular project. Also, no progress has been made on mapping the interior of Nedderman Hall. This has led us to re-evaluate our development plan, more on this can be found in the Development Plan section.

# **What was Accomplished in Iteration 1?**

Our current deliverable is a working iOS and Android app given the user runs it through Expo. It contains 4 notable pages each with decent work done.

* Map: shows a hand traced map of the campus bounded by S Cooper St, UTA Blvd, S Center St, and W Mitchell, 37 buildings and residence halls, 16 parking lots, though only 7 are usable by students, and the 4 aforementioned streets. Tapping a building opens up a preview of the building and a little more information about it.  
* Schedule: shows the user's classes sorted by start time, with each one labeled Upcoming, In Progress, or Done based on the current time. Users can add a class through a form or remove one with a confirmation prompt. Tapping a class opens a detail screen with a placeholder for turn by turn routing coming in iteration 2\.  
* Parking: shows a copy of the map but with buildings grayed out and parking lots highlighted as the main center of attention. Users can select different parking permit types to see which lots they are allowed to park in. Accessible lots are highlighted in green, while restricted lots appear in red.   
* Settings: allows users to access their profile where they can manually enter and remove classes from their schedule, and select their parking permit. Under app customization users can switch between light and dark themes. There are also options to choose time zones, and select preferred distance units they want their app in but their implementation will come later. Also, created icon designs for the Map, Schedule, Parking, and Settings tabs to improve the appearance of the bottom navigation bar. 

# **Development Plan**

As we began development of the project, we realized some goals may be a bit too ambitious for the given time and have readjusted our plans to increase the likelihood we meet our deadlines. We have also decided to split our project into “sub-iterations” to tackle some more features.

| Iteration | Due Date | Milestone |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 (Current) | 09/20/26 | Working app on both iOS and Android. Outdoor map render of a portion of campus made as well as supported parking lots, manual schedule input, and certain settings features. |
| 1.5 | 10/04/26 | Remaining outdoor campus traced. Choose a starting point (residence halls and apartments, US-04). Outdoor routing from a lot or residence to a building. Parking recommendation from the permit and the first class all done. |
| 2 | 10/11/26 | Working schedule implementation. Implemented Nedderman Hall, Engineering Research Building, and Woolf Hall’s indoor navigation feature. |
| 2.5 | 10/25/26 | Implemented all buildings right of Cooper’s indoor navigation feature. Add avoid high foot traffic areas option. |
| 3 | 11/01/26 | Remainder of campus mapped out and MyMav schedule parser included. Make the app no longer require a person running Expo through a tunnel (make it standalone). |
| 4 | 11/15/26 | Any changes required for final delivery. Aesthetics improvement and minor changes. |

Our interviews ranked indoor navigation as the biggest pain point, but an indoor route starts at a building entrance, and the outdoor map, schedule, and parking permit filters are what get a student there. We therefore built the map and its dependent features first, so the indoor work sits on a stable base. Iteration 2 will introduce this feature and carries our highest data unknown risk (R-08 explained later). By validating our coordinate projection and custom SVG rendering for Iteration 1 and 1.5, we will have a stable architecture before introducing complex multi floor navigation algorithms.

Iteration 1 focused exclusively on outdoor campus mapping, user schedule input, and permit filtered parking visualization before working on indoor navigation. This sequence minimizes the amount of backtracking we will have to do in future iterations and sets us up to implement indoor navigation of the buildings in Iteration 2\. Iteration 2 also aims to fully separate us from our competitors because at the moment, we have no differentiating factors between them.

# **Competitor Reality Check**

With our current iteration delivery, we do not have anything that sets us apart from major competitors. We have a stationary map of a portion of UTA which is beaten out by the online UTA map as well as the static PDF map \[3, 7\]. We have support for some parking lots which are beaten out by Modii \[4, 7\]. However, we have set ourselves up to be able to create uniqueness from our competitors by iteration 2\. In Iteration 1, we added support for the user to manually input their own schedule. This is going to be what sets us apart. By iteration two, there will be a working schedule with time of day support and outdoor navigation to go along with it, and for the three buildings we plan to support by iteration 2, there will also be indoor navigation for the buildings.

# **Competitor Uniqueness**

| Feature / Capability | Google Maps \[7\] | UTA Static PDF  \[3, 7\] | Modii (PATS Portal) \[4, 7\] | Mavigator |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Outdoor Pedestrian Paths | Yes (Generic) | No (Static visual) | No | Planned (Iteration 1.5) |
| Permit-Filtered Parking | No | No | Partial (Live counts only) | Yes (Permit & time of day) |
| Personal Schedule Integration | No | No | No | Planned (Iteration 2\) |
| Indoor Room Navigation | No | No | No | Planned (Iteration 2\) |
| Offline / Client-Only Execution | No | Yes | No | Yes (Client-Side Rendering) |

Google Maps \[7\] is the app most people we interviewed already use. It’s great for getting to campus but stops at the building's front door. It has no ability to help the user navigate indoors and through multiple floors or know the user’s parking permit. The UTA PDF \[3, 7\] map shows every building as well as parking similar to Modii \[4, 7\] but does not allow the user to have their classes imported and guide them.

# **Risk Evaluation**

With this iteration, we have identified and introduced two new risks, and both of them appear in the Top 5 risks. R-08 and R-09 as seen below.

| Risk ID | Risk Description | Category | Probability | Impact (hours) | Risk Exposure | Mitigation (more below) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| R-08 (new) | Indoor plans for buildings at UTA | External Data | 60% | 20 | 12.0 | Request UTA floor plans, otherwise map by hand |
| R-01 | Remodel or demolition of a building | External Data | 50% | 8 | 4.0 | Focus indoor mapping to more established buildings |
| R-09 (new) | Hand-traced map differs or drifts from the real campus | Technical | 40% | 8 | 3.2 | Be as precise as possible when tracing the map’s nodes |
| R-02 | Construction of new building | External Data | 50% | 5 | 2.5 | Be ready to map out the newly constructed building |
| R-04 | Not able to map certain locations | External Data | 70% | 3 | 2.1 | Mark unfinished buildings as “not yet supported” |

We have decided that these risks were the most predominant risks. 4 out of 5 of our top risks are External Data risks meaning we do not have a real means of being able to eliminate them as possible risks, but we have means of mitigating them.

# **Detailed Mitigation of Risks**

**R-08 (floor plans)**: UTA keeps room-level plans in its CASIM system \[3\], and access is by request through Facilities Management (ofm@uta.edu). We will send that request as a CSE 3311 class project and hand-map Nedderman Hall Floor 1 from on-site measurement by 10/1 so Iteration 2 is not behind. If CASIM access arrives, we replace the hand data. If not, we ship the hand-mapped floors and mark other buildings "not yet supported," which is the fallback from R-04.

**R-01 / R-02 (building changes)**: We map only established buildings indoors and keep footprints in one data file, so correcting a building is a one-file change. All that is required is an outdoor measurement of the building and indoor mapping.

**R-09 (accuracy)**: This one already happened once. Our first trace, taken from the UTA PDF, was incorrectly measured from the OpenStreetView map. We discarded it and re-traced from satellite imagery with our own digitizer tool \[6\]. The remaining mitigation is a data test that blocks shapes outside the campus boundaries plus a visual spot check of five buildings every iteration.

**R-04 (unmappable locations)**: Areas we cannot get floor plans for, such as staff-only rooms or buildings UTA does not release, are shown as "not yet supported" instead of being routed incorrectly.

**R-03 (platforms)**: All features were checked by hand on iOS and Android. The development framework we chose unified the development between the two platforms and mitigated the risk so we lowered the expected time to fix these types of issues.

# **Risk That Became Reality**

**R-07 (API switch)**: During this iteration, we encountered a risk that came true. During our inception, we defined R-07 as a risk that could occur if we need to switch map API. It was an exposure of 1.5, but was grossly underestimated. We decided to drop Google Maps API in favor of our own SVG map. It took about 3 hours of tracing and will require many more hours manually tracing the remainder of campus as well as defining entrance to buildings. However, doing this allows us to remove API key billing and dependencies.

| Schedule | Current schedule from settings Tap Add Class Form entries (course, code, building, room, time) Tap a class to view details Tap Remove, then confirm The phone’s clock | Add Class form opens New class added in time order Class detail screen opens Class removed from list Each class marked Done, In Progress, or Upcoming |
| Parking | Selected permit (from the "Selected Pass" button or from Settings) One finger drag.  Two finger pinch.  Opening or returning to the Parking tab.  | Allowed lots appear green, restricted lots red, and commuter lots that open at 1 PM yellow. After 7 PM and on weekends every lot is green for any permit. Parking lot colors update when the selected permit changes.  Map moves and zooms based on user interaction.  The map automatically focuses on the parking lots when opened. |
| Settings | Select parking permit Manually input schedule Selected theme (Light/Dark) Select time format and time zone Select distance measurement units | Selected permit is used by the Parking tab Classes appear on the Schedule tab App appearance updates to the selected theme Time format and time zone are saved for the session. Displayed times do not change yet Distance unit is saved for the session. No distances are shown yet. |

# **Key Data Structures**

**Coordinate** { lat, lng } is a single position type. It stores real latitude and longitude as floats to be projected onto our SVG map even though the map is drawn on a flat canvas, so later when we switch to a real map software development kit, the data will not require re-entering.

**PointOfInterest** is a building or residence: id, name, category (academic, residence, apartment), a coordinate, an abbreviation (e.g. NH), footprint (a polygon of coordinates). Each building is identified by its string id. The abbreviation is what students see on schedules and door signs, so it is how a class will be linked to a building. We use it instead of UTA's numeric building codes \[3\] because UTA no longer publishes codes for new buildings \[3\].

**CampusLot** (id, label, coordinate, footprint) and CampusStreet (id, name, path) are drawn for context and used for the Parking tab. A lot's id is also the key the permit rules use, so the map and the rules cannot disagree about which lot is which.

**ParkingPermit** is one of nine permits (East Commuter, Preferred Garage, etc). The user's choice can also be None. The choice is kept in a shared store, parkingPermitStore, so the Parking tab and Settings always agree. getParkingPermission(permit, lotId, time) returns allowed, restricted, or timeRestricted for a lot \[4\], and PARKING\_COLORS turns that into green, red, or yellow on the map. The time is a parameter so the rules can be tested at any hour.

**ScheduleClass** represents a saved class: id, courseCode, courseName, buildingCode, roomNumber, startTime, endTime, completed, and a status of done, upcoming, or normal calculated from the current time. The full list of ScheduleClass entries is kept in shared state rather than saved to disk, so the Schedule tab and the Settings tab's schedule editor read and update the same data. buildingCode holds the building's abbreviation (e.g. NH). A class already in progress keeps the status upcoming with 0 minutes remaining. The class list lives in a ScheduleProvider that both tabs read.

**Shared settings** (src/state) are two small stores shared across pages: the selected parking permit (parkingPermitStore) and the theme preference (themePreferenceStore, set with setThemePreference: system, light, or dark). The schedule is shared through ScheduleProvider (src/context) with addClass() and removeClass(). The time format, time zone, and distance unit choices are currently local to their own screens. All of this is kept for the current session only.

**MapNode, MapEdge, Route** are the routing graphs. A MapNode is a junction (entrance, hallway, corner, lot gate). A MapEdge joins two nodes with a distance and a walkable flag. A Route is the ordered nodes and edges Dijkstra will return, with appropriate distances and ETAs. They are defined now so that Iteration 2 is prepared for (they are not currently in use).

**Projection** converts a Coordinate into the map’s flat drawing space. The map’s bounding box must match the one used by our tracing tool, or shapes will appear stretched.

# **Exceptional Cases Handled**

* Releasing your finger while dragging on top of a building does not open the detailed breakdown of the building  
* Dragging past the campus edge stops at the edge  
* Settings menu buttons with no implementation yet are shown disabled  
* No parking permit selected does not allow parking in any lots  
* Parking after 7PM on weekdays and on weekends are open to anyone with a permit  
* When the current class is removed, the next one becomes upcoming  
* Add Class rejects a form with an empty field ("Please fill in all fields")  
* Removing a class asks for confirmation

# **Cases We do Not Handle Yet**

* Add Class does not reject an ending time before the start time or vice versa  
* Add Class accepts any building and class numbers  
* Nothing is saved between launches  
* Indoor navigation through multiple floors or real time GPS data  
* Time format, time zone, and distance unit choices do not change the display yet  
* Parking colors show what a permit may use, not whether a lot has spaces

# **Consistency With Inception Documents**

* The lot detail screen (tap a lot for status and recommendation) is not built yet  
* Route previews are placeholders and have no function right now  
* Permit rules are from UTA’s parking map \[4\] and not confirmed  
* US-01 also lists Staff Parking, time of year, and walking ETA. Iteration 1 offers nine student permits, and the walking ETA is planned for Iteration 1.5.

# Code and Tests

Features reflect real user priorities and work. The most complex code has comments and the most important code has appropriate tests. Organization matches the domain and no unneeded code is present (with the exception of stubs and future development of iterations). Original Expo assets \[1\] are still present for loading reasons only. Once we eliminate the default loading screen, the assets will be removed too.

# **Features vs. User Feedback**

Our primary users are UTA Commuter students as well as on campus residents. Our primary customers are UTA students (beneficiaries of reduced navigation time) and our course evaluators (assessing our software delivery).

Our five inception interviews pointed to three problems. A majority of students said they get lost inside buildings or find room numbers confusing, which is our top priority and the first task of Iteration 2\. Commuters (Tan Nguyen, Andy Ta) struggled to find parking that fits their permit, which is why the Parking tab filters lots by permit. On-campus residents (Blaine Smith) wanted to start routes from their residence, which is planned for Iteration 1.5. On 9/19/26, we showed the Iteration 1 build to Tan and Blaine. They said "looks good but i wouldnt use it rn" and “you forgot my apartment”. These heavily inspired the redo of our development plan to the current iterations seen earlier. They also said the app would not yet be useful to them without indoor navigation, which is why that is our next milestone.

# **Complex Code and its Components**

* Pinch-zoom and pan path keeps the point under the user’s fingers fixed while zooming \[2\]. It also limits the zoom to 0.6x to 4x and stops panning at the edge of campus. It was pulled out of the React component into pure functions so it can be tested without a phone.  
* Tap guard prevents the opening of a building’s details if the user lets go of their finger right above a building while panning. The guard ignores gestures for 250ms after panning.  
* Permit rules turn a permit, a lot, and the time into a color. It also updates depending on the time of day provided by the user’s phone.  
* Schedule logic sorts classes and marks each done, upcoming, or normal based on the time of day provided by the user’s phone. Time entry utilizes the native datetimepicker \[2\].  
* Projection converts latitude and longitude into drawing space and is shared by the map and the building preview so they cannot differ.  
* Campus bounds must equal the tracing tool's box, or every shape is stretched. This mistake has happened during development.

# **Tests:**

The code has 12 test files and 151 tests, all passing. TypeScript type checking and lint also pass with no errors.

| Test file | What it checks |
| :---- | :---- |
| projection.test.ts | The center and corners are converted correctly during projection. North is up, East is right |
| map-geometry.test.ts | Zoom keeps the point under the fingers fixed, zoom clamps to 0.6x to 4x, and the map cannot be dragged past the campus edge |
| map-viewport.test.ts | Saved view carries between screen sizes and tabs and stays in bounds |
| tap-guard.test.ts | Releasing a drag over a building doesn't open it, but a real tap does. |
| campus-data.test.ts | Buildings, lots, and streets have unique ids, shapes with at least 3 points, and coordinates inside the campus box. |
| parking-permits.test.ts | Which lots each of the nine permits may use, with no permit selected everything is restricted, the 1 PM commuter switch, and the weekend and after 7 PM opening. Every lot drawn on the map has a rule. |
| parking-permit-options.test.tsx | The permit choices and the pull-up sheet on the Parking tab. The sheet and Settings stay in sync through the same saved choice. |
| schedule-context.test.tsx | Schedule logic, time parsing, chronological order, adding and removing classes, and marking each class done, upcoming or normal at different times of day. |
| class-list-item.test.tsx | The class card, flag colors, "In progress" and "Upcoming class" never showing together, the done check, and the status glow. |
| manual-add-class-form.test.tsx | The Add Class form shows every field, and its pull-up sheet opens and closes. |
| time-format.test.ts | The time picker text, 5 minute steps, 12-hour format including noon and midnight, and rejecting text that is not a time. |
| state.test.ts | The shared settings, the permit starts as None and the theme starts by following the device, and changes reach every screen using them. |

| schedule/ | src/components/ | Schedule class cards and the Add Class form |

# How to Run the Code

You need [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/) (v24 was used to develop it) and, to run it on a phone, the **Expo Go** app \[1\] from the App Store or Google Play.

Run the following commands:  
Please note that if tunnel does not work, you may need to sign in to an account on both your phone and the CLI used to host the app.

`git clone https://github.com/AntoVu/cse3311-fall26-group7.git`  
`cd cse3311-fall26-group7`  
`npm install`  
`npx expo login`  
`npx expo start --tunnel`

In the terminal that opens:

* **Phone:** scan the QR code. If not using \--tunnel flag, both devices need to be on the same network.  
* **Browser:** the tabs were checked in a browser early in Iteration 1, but the app is designed for a phone, so use a phone as the reference.

# **Running Tests**

Run the following command

`npm test`

Expected result: 12 test files and 151 tests passed. A manual checklist for each tab is in the repository's README.md.

This runs [Jest](https://jestjs.io/) (via jest-expo). Unit tests are next to the code they test, in a \_\_tests\_\_ folder.
